capabilities: Read notes aloud with chunked, gapless playback and per-note resume
Trigger playback from selected sentences, right-click, or the command palette
Queue reading of a folder or backlinks and jump between chunks
Strip or toggle markdown elements like code blocks, tables, and parentheses before speaking
Export the spoken note as a single WAV file into the vault
extras: Not yet available in the community plugin store; install manually or via BRAT. The author's ttsd server is recommended as an option. Defaults to Korean voices (omnivoice model, Korean-Female-Eunji voice).
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to listen to notes as spoken audio, so reading long notes hands-free requires an external tool.

relations.evidence: OpenVox (recommended, macOS) — openvoxai.com. Free app that exposes the /v1 endpoints this plugin uses
ttsd — my own self-hosted TTS server speaking the same /v1 contract

requires.name: local OpenAI-compatible TTS server (e.g. OpenVox or ttsd)

summary: Text-to-speech player that reads markdown notes aloud through a local OpenAI-compatible TTS server, with chunked gapless playback and WAV export.
